subject: pathology
title: Apoptosis Mechanisms, Death Receptors, and the Extrinsic Pathway

steps.tx: Unlike necrosis which represents accidental, unregulated cell lysis accompanied by intense inflammation, programmed cell death operates through an energy-dependent molecular suicide program. Designated **apoptosis**, this pathway orchestrates controlled cellular shrinkage, chromatin condensation, membrane blebbing, and fragmentation into membrane-bound apoptotic bodies without inciting tissue inflammation.
steps.say: Apoptosis is programmed cell death that eliminates cells quietly into apoptotic bodies without inflammation.

vis.caption: Interface hepatitis demonstrating individual hepatocyte apoptosis into condensed Councilman bodies.
vis.alt: Autoimmune hepatitis showing individual hepatocyte apoptotic bodies

steps.tx: Apoptosis plays essential homeostatic roles in both physiological and pathological contexts. During embryogenesis, apoptosis sculpts digits by eliminating interdigital webbing, maintains constant cell numbers in proliferating tissues, and deletes autoreactive T-lymphocytes during **central thymic tolerance**, while also removing virally infected and DNA-damaged cells.
steps.say: Apoptosis removes interdigital webbing in embryos, deletes autoreactive T cells, and culls damaged cells.

left.title: Physiological Apoptosis Roles
points: Cell turnover in proliferating epithelia (intestinal crypt migration)
Deletion of self-reactive lymphocytes during central negative selection

right.title: Pathological Apoptosis Roles
points: DNA damage response following ionizing radiation or chemotherapy
Cellular death induced by accumulation of misfolded ER proteins
Elimination of virus-infected cells by cytotoxic T-lymphocytes
Pathological organ atrophy following duct obstruction (pancreas, kidney)

steps.tx: The decision to execute apoptosis can be initiated through two distinct converging molecular arms: the intrinsic mitochondrial pathway and the extrinsic death receptor pathway. In the **intrinsic mitochondrial pathway**, intracellular stresses such as DNA damage, growth factor deprivation, or oxidative injury trigger mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization.
steps.say: The intrinsic apoptotic pathway triggers mitochondrial permeabilization in response to internal stress.

nodes.label: DNA Double-Strand Breaks or Growth Factor Withdrawal Triggers Sensor Activation
BH3-Only Proteins (BIM, PUMA, NOXA) Neutralize Anti-Apoptotic BCL-2
Pro-Apoptotic BAX and BAK Oligomerize in Outer Mitochondrial Membrane
Cytochrome C Discharges into Cytosol to Activate Apaf-1 and Caspase-9

steps.tx: Conversely, the extrinsic apoptotic pathway is triggered by extracellular ligand binding to specialized cell-surface death receptors belonging to the tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily. In this **extrinsic death receptor pathway**, receptors such as Fas (CD95) and tumor necrosis factor receptor-one contain an intracellular eighty amino acid death domain that organizes apoptotic complexes.
steps.say: The extrinsic pathway uses cell surface death receptors like Fas to trigger apoptosis from outside signals.

steps.tx: A quintessential trigger of the extrinsic apoptotic pathway is the interaction between the cell-surface receptor Fas and its cognate ligand. Expressed on activated cytotoxic T-lymphocytes and natural killer cells, **Fas ligand binding** induces trimerization of Fas receptors on target cells, clustering their intracellular death domains.
steps.say: Fas ligand on cytotoxic T cells binds and trimerizes target Fas receptors to initiate death signaling.

nodes.label: Cytotoxic CD8+ T-Cell Presents Membrane-Bound Fas Ligand (CD178)
Cross-Links and Trimerizes Fas (CD95) Receptors on Target Cell Membrane
Clustered Death Domains Recruit Adapter Protein FADD via Homotypic Binding
Assembles Death-Inducing Signaling Complex (DISC) to Cleave Procaspase-8

steps.tx: Clustered intracellular death domains recruit an adapter protein designated Fas-associated death domain protein. Together with procaspase-eight, this assembly forms the **death-inducing signaling complex**, which brings multiple inactive initiator procaspases into close proximity, enabling mutual autoproteolytic cleavage into active initiator caspase-eight.
steps.say: The death-inducing signaling complex aggregates and cleaves procaspase-8 into its active initiator form.

left.title: DISC Assembly Components
points: Trimerized Fas (CD95) or TRAIL death receptor complexes
FADD (Fas-Associated Death Domain) bridging adapter protein
Drives induced proximity and autocatalytic caspase activation

right.title: FLIP Inhibition Mechanism
points: Cellular FLIP (c-FLIP) binds FADD via death effector domains
Competitively blocks procaspase-8 recruitment to the DISC
Overexpressed by tumor cells and viruses to resist immune attack

steps.tx: Active caspase-eight serves as the key molecular bridge connecting the extrinsic death receptor pathway directly to executioner caspases. Additionally, caspase-eight can cleave the pro-apoptotic BH3-only protein BID into **truncated BID**, which translocates to mitochondria to activate BAX and engage the intrinsic pathway, amplifying the apoptotic signal.
steps.say: Caspase-8 cleaves BID into truncated BID, recruiting the mitochondrial pathway to amplify apoptosis.

nodes.label: Active Caspase-8 Directly Cleaves Executioner Procaspases-3 and 7
Concurrently Cleaves Cytosolic Full-Length BID into Truncated BID (tBID)
tBID Translocates to Mitochondria to Activate BAX and BAK Oligomers
Engages Intrinsic Pathway, Ensuring Irreversible Apoptotic Commitment

steps.tx: Once activated, executioner caspases cleave structural and regulatory intracellular substrates, culminating in cell disassembly into membrane-bound fragments termed apoptotic bodies. These bodies rapidly display **phosphatidylserine on outer membranes**, signaling resident tissue phagocytes to engulf them immediately, preventing leakage of intracellular contents and avoiding tissue inflammation.
steps.say: Apoptotic bodies expose phosphatidylserine on their surface to prompt rapid non-inflammatory phagocytosis.

Activates Scramblase, Flipping Phosphatidylserine to Outer Membrane Leaflet
Extracellular Phosphatidylserine Acts as a Universal 'Eat-Me' Flag
Macrophage Receptors Engulf Apoptotic Bodies Completely Within Minutes
